draft.title: Emotional development
card: Emotional development is how a person learns to recognise, express and manage emotions. It starts in infancy and continues through childhood and adolescence.
a close emotional bond between an infant and a carer. A carer who responds warmly and reliably helps the infant feel safe and learn that emotions can be soothed.

Children learn to name feelings, such as anger or pride, and to read them in other people. With help from adults, they begin to manage strong feelings, for example by asking for help instead of lashing out.
Teenagers face stronger and more mixed feelings. They can use more strategies to manage them, such as thinking about a problem in a different way or talking it through with a friend.
draft.remember: Emotional development is learning to recognise, express and manage emotions, and early attachment is where it begins.

a.q: Which example shows a child managing an emotion?
opts: Taking deep breaths to calm down before a spelling test
Saying that a friend looks sad after losing a game
Crying loudly when a parent leaves the room
Smiling at a carer who comes into the room
a.why: Taking deep breaths is a way to change how a feeling affects the child, so it is managing an emotion. Saying a friend looks sad is recognising an emotion, which is a different part of emotional development.
a.clue: Managing means doing something to handle a feeling.

b.q: Priya is 15 and feels furious after an unfair mark. She waits until she has calmed down, then talks it through with a friend. What does this show?
opts: Using a strategy to manage her anger
Failing to form an attachment in infancy
Hiding an emotion so that nobody can see it
Recognising an emotion in another person
b.why: Priya waits and talks it through, which are strategies for handling her anger. It is not hiding the emotion, because she still talks openly about it with a friend. The feeling is her own, so it is not recognising an emotion in another person.
b.clue: Look at what Priya does with her own feeling.

a.best: Taking deep breaths to calm down before a spelling test

b.best: Using a strategy to manage her anger
